title: Azure Storage Overview
description: Learn about Azure Storage accounts, the core resource that holds all your blobs, files, queues, tables, and disks.

data.text: Azure Storage is Microsoft's cloud storage solution for modern applications. A single **storage account** acts as a namespace that gives you access to multiple storage services: blobs for unstructured data, files for cloud or on-premises file shares, queues for messaging, tables for NoSQL key-value data, and managed disks for virtual machines.

Think of a storage account like a digital warehouse. It has a unique name, lives inside an Azure resource group, and provides a set of endpoints your apps can call. Everything you store — images, logs, virtual hard drives — goes into a storage account.

data.title: Create a Storage Account with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision a new general-purpose v2 storage account
data.code:
az group create --name rg-demo --location eastus
az storage account create \
  --name stdemostorage \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

terms.definition: A top-level Azure resource that provides a unique namespace and access to all storage services.
A logical container for Azure resources that share the same lifecycle, permissions, and policies.
A URL that applications use to reach a specific storage service inside a storage account.
A pricing and replication tier (e.g., Standard_LRS, Premium_ZRS) that determines cost and durability.

data.title: General-Purpose v2
data.text: Use StorageV2 (general-purpose v2) for most new projects. It supports all storage services, hot/cool/archive tiers, and modern features like soft delete and private links.

data.caption: A storage account contains multiple storage services.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Storage Account] --> B[Blob Storage]
    A --> C[Azure Files]
    A --> D[Queue Storage]
    A --> E[Table Storage]
    A --> F[Managed Disks]

data.title: Exercise: Explore the Azure Portal
data.description: Provision a storage account and explore its services in the Azure Portal.
steps: Open the Azure Portal and create a new resource group.
Create a storage account named <yourname>storage with the Standard_LRS SKU.
Navigate to the storage account and note the endpoint URLs under Settings > Endpoints.
List the available services in the left navigation.
data.expectedOutcome: A working storage account with visible service endpoints in the portal.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Storage organizes data into storage accounts.
A single account can host blobs, files, queues, tables, and managed disks.
StorageV2 is the recommended account type for new projects.
Endpoints give your apps a URL to reach each storage service.
data.takeaway: You now understand the Azure Storage account as the foundation for every storage service you will use as a developer.
